domain: Technology History / Economic Sociology / Path Dependence Theory
topic_summary: Analysis of QWERTY keyboard layout persistence examining whether its dominance represents natural technical optimization, deliberate manufacturer lock-in strategy, or path-dependent emergence without clear beneficiaries. The topic tests whether beneficiary-hunting analytical frameworks construct beneficiaries artifactually or discover them structurally.

key_entities: E. Remington and Sons (manufacturer, 1873 rights purchaser)
Dvorak layout (1930s ergonomic alternative, never adopted)
Paul David (path dependence theorist, inefficiency argument)
Liebowitz & Margolis (efficiency defenders, 'Fable of the Keys' authors)
key_tensions: Technical necessity (jam prevention) vs strategic design (training lock-in)
Path dependence with multiple equilibria (David) vs single efficient outcome (Liebowitz/Margolis)
Naturalization narrative (QWERTY looks inevitable) vs constructed persistence (beneficiaries maintain it)
key_mechanisms: Typist training investment creating switching costs
Manufacturer standardization via Union Typewriter Company cartel (1893)
Employer dependence on existing skilled labor pool
key_absences: Direct evidence of deliberate anti-competitive intent by Remington
Controlled ergonomic comparison data from adoption period (pre-1930s Dvorak)

commitment_system_recognition.collapse_reason: Readings do not emit structurally different constraints—they emit different EXPLANATIONS for the same observable constraint (QWERTY dominance). The constraint itself (switching cost, training investment requirement, manufacturer standardization) is identical across readings. What differs is the CAUSAL STORY (accident vs design vs emergence) and the NORMATIVE FRAMING (efficient vs inefficient), not the constraint structure. This is observer-position disagreement about one constraint, not multiple constraints from one kernel.
commitment_system_recognition.analytical_note: The D3 artifact warning is valid: beneficiary-hunting frameworks risk constructing beneficiaries where structural analysis finds only path-dependent emergence. The 'beneficiary reading' and 'no-beneficiary reading' are not two constraints but two interpretations of switching-cost lock-in. Decomposing into ordinary axes with the beneficiary question as an omega variable.

omegas.description: Does switching_cost_lock_in have a beneficiary, or does beneficiary-hunting construct one artifactually? Three candidate answers: (1) No beneficiary—pure path dependence, training externality creates lock-in without strategic actors. (2) Emergent beneficiary—Remington/Union Typewriter gained from lock-in but did not design it. (3) Designed beneficiary—manufacturers deliberately exploited training costs (Remington training courses claim). Evidence for (3) is thin (no smoking-gun anti-competitive intent documents). Evidence for (1) vs (2) depends on whether 'gaining from' equals 'benefiting from' in constraint ontology. The D3 artifact warning applies: if the analytical framework requires finding a beneficiary, it will construct Remington as strategic actor even if lock-in was accidental.
omegas.source: User's D3 ARTIFACT flag + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + deferred axis ergonomic_efficiency_delta

omegas.description: Is QWERTY actually inefficient (David) or approximately optimal given historical constraints (Liebowitz/Margolis)? If Liebowitz/Margolis are correct, typist_training_externality is a Mountain (layout-specific skill is unavoidable) and switching_cost_lock_in is a Rope (coordination on any standard beats fragmentation). If David is correct, switching_cost_lock_in is a Snare (inferior equilibrium maintained by coordination failure). Empirical evidence is contested; no controlled ergonomic studies from adoption period exist.
omegas.source: Deferred axis ergonomic_efficiency_delta + scholarly dispute between David and Liebowitz/Margolis

omegas.description: Did Remington design QWERTY to be non-intuitive to create training-course revenue and lock-in (beneficiary reading), or was layout choice driven by jam prevention and typist feedback with lock-in as unintended consequence (no-beneficiary reading)? The 'Remington training courses' claim appears in secondary sources but lacks primary documentation. If true, it evidences strategic exploitation of switching costs. If false or exaggerated, it exemplifies beneficiary-construction artifact. The constraint (switching cost) exists either way; the beneficiary attribution is the variable.
omegas.source: User's kernel contest framing + absence of direct evidence for deliberate anti-competitive intent

omegas.description: Is typist_training_externality a true Mountain (cognitive/motor learning is inherently layout-specific) or a Piton (layout-specificity is a training method choice)? Modern touch-typing pedagogy assumes layout-specificity, but this may be self-fulfilling. If layout-general typing skill is learnable, the Mountain collapses to a Piton of pedagogical convention, and switching_cost_lock_in becomes a Snare maintained by training industry inertia rather than cognitive necessity.
omegas.source: F03 (Hasty Generalization) + Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)
